commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Five R2.2 document templates added — KES, Ontwerptoelichting, Objectenboom, Bevindingenformulier, Hoeveelheidsbepaling
details: One template per green “Format …” box in R2_2 - VO.pdf: KES, Ontwerptoelichting, Objectenboom, Bevindingenformulier and Hoeveelheidsbepaling. A Format in the diagram and a `.document` in LDE are the same thing — a template with bindings — so the mapping is direct; the blue outputs beside them in the spec are instances of these templates rather than artifacts of their own.

Zone keys are `signOff` and `contactInformation`, camelCase, from the start — unlike R2.1's templates, which shipped with `signoff` and `contactInfo`, keys `DocumentZones` never declares, leaving their signature blocks unrendered until 49832d2 repaired them.
Completes the RipR22Process bundle: the manifest now declares nothing that does not exist, and the fixture suite is green.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Nine R2.2 user task forms added, one per lane task, bound by camunda:formRef
details: One form per user task in RipR22Process. Field types stay inside the eight the R2.1 bundle already uses — text, textarea, textfield, checkbox, datetime, select, radio, button — since nothing else is exercised against this Camunda 7.21 stack.

The spec's conditional “LCC-raming (indien variantenafweging)” is modelled as a checkbox plus a reference field on `rip-concept-vo.form` rather than an artifact of its own, since it only exists when a variant trade-off happened.

`klicMeldingReferentie` is collected only on `rip-inventariseren-kabels-leidingen.form`. The concept VO task reads the same information but does not also write it, since two forms writing one process variable would mean whichever task completes last silently wins.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: R2.2 document templates were unattached — RipR22Process shipped without ronl:documentRef
details: R2.1 wires each document template to the task that produces it with `ronl:documentRef` — the attribute `DocumentTemplateSelector` writes and `BpmnCanvas` reads to render the document badge on a task in the Modeler. The R2.2 spec never mentioned it, so RipR22Process shipped without it and the five templates added alongside it would have imported but attached to nothing.

The attribute is single-valued, so a task can carry at most one template. Four of the five bind: Task_VerzamelenKlanteisen → rip-kes, Task_OpstellenConceptVO → rip-ontwerptoelichting, Task_BesprekenConceptVO → rip-bevindingenformulier, Task_OpstellenDefinitiefVO → rip-hoeveelheidsbepaling. `rip-objectenboom` stays unattached on purpose — Task_OpstellenConceptVO produces both the Ontwerptoelichting and the Objectenboom, and its one slot went to the Ontwerptoelichting; the Objectenboom still ships and imports normally, it simply carries no task badge. Its reference is additionally maintained in Relatics.
Values are bare template ids with no `.document` suffix, matching R2.1. Both the `examples/` and `e2e-fixtures/` copies are updated so the parity test stays green.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: RipR22Process added — four lanes, nine user tasks, from R2_2 - VO.pdf
details: Four lanes and nine user tasks from R2_2 - VO.pdf (rev. 21-11-2024), picking up where RipR21Process's “Fase 1 voltooid → R2.2” end event left off.

All five branches of the opening parallel split rejoin the join gateway. The PDF does not draw it that way — it shows Inventariseren kabels en leidingen and Aanvragen raamvergunning leaving the pool into CO1 and JU3.5 and never coming back, which as control flow deadlocks at the join. Those hand-offs are `textAnnotation`s instead: CO1 and JU3.5 do not exist as fixtures, so a `callActivity` would dangle at deploy time and fail the manifest's `calledElement` test. They are referenced by several phases and belong in a shared bundle of their own.
The manifest entry declares the nine forms and five documents that the following commits add, so the fixture suite's file-existence test stays red until the bundle is complete.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: New parity test locks each RIP bundle's examples/ and e2e-fixtures/ copies together
details: Each RIP bundle exists twice on disk: authored under `examples/`, imported and deployed from `e2e-fixtures/`. Nothing stopped the two drifting, and they have — 49832d2 repaired the document zone keys in the `e2e-fixtures` copies only, and the `examples` copies kept the dead `signoff`/`contactInfo` keys until 44d1cb4 re-pasted them by hand.
A new test asserts every file in a mirrored bundle is byte-identical to its twin. New bundles opt in by adding an entry to `MIRRORED_BUNDLES`.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: rip-phase1-swimlanes renamed to rip-phase-21
details: The `-swimlanes` suffix distinguished this bundle from a competing `rip-phase1/` draft that b1b88a8 deleted, so it now distinguishes nothing, and the directory name no longer matched the process it holds (RipR21Process). Renaming it makes the incoming R2.2 bundle an obvious sibling: `rip-phase-21/` holds RipR21Process, `rip-phase-22/` holds RipR22Process.

Contents are untouched. Exactly one reference to the old path existed — the `source` field of the RipR21Process entry in `e2e-fixtures/manifest.json` — and it is repointed here. Nothing resolves this directory at runtime; the app serves examples from `packages/frontend/public/examples/`, which has never held the RIP bundles.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: bump-release now versions the lockfile, not just package.json
details: The release step said “set `version` in each in-scope package.json” and nothing more, so no release ever touched `package-lock.json`. Through v2026.08.2 it still recorded the root at `1.9.13` and `packages/backend` at `0.1.0`, while every `package.json` in the repo had reached `2026.08.2`.

The step now uses `npm version <ver> --no-git-tag-version`, once for the root and once per in-scope workspace, which writes each `package.json` and its lockfile entry together. The drift was never fatal — `npm ci` validates dependency satisfiability, and the root depends on its workspaces by path rather than by version range, so those `version` fields are never checked — but the lockfile is what CI installs from and what SBOM, audit and provenance tooling reads, so all of it reported the wrong versions.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: E2E fixture BPMNs were undeployable — artifacts placed before flow elements
details: BPMN 2.0’s `tProcess` is an ordered sequence — `laneSet*`, `flowElement*`, `artifact*`, `resourceRole*`, `correlationSubscription*`, `supports*` — so once an artifact appears, no further flow element may follow it. Operaton validates against the XSD on deploy and rejects the entire deployment when it doesn’t hold, with `cvc-complex-type.2.4.a: Invalid content was found starting with element '{…}:scriptTask'`.

The commit that added the on-canvas “E2E FIXTURE” warning inserted its `textAnnotation` and `association` directly after the first flow element, leaving four of the five fixtures undeployable. Each banner moves to just before `</bpmn:process>`, matching `TreeFellingPermitSubProcessE2E` — the one file that had it right and the only one that deployed. A pure move: no content changes, DI untouched, and all five now validate against `bpmn-moddle`’s `BPMN20.xsd`.

Nothing caught this because the integrity test checked file existence, process ids and `calledElement` references but never whether the BPMN was deployable at all. These fixtures are hand-edited and never round-trip through bpmn-js, which would have re-serialised them into schema order and silently repaired the mistake. A fifth test now asserts the ordering rule directly.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: BPMN process key was always the literal string “process”
details: `doc.querySelector('process')` is a CSS *type* selector, which matches only the null namespace — so it never found the `<bpmn:process>` element that real bpmn-js output always emits, and all four call sites in `BpmnCanvas` fell through to their own fallbacks every time. Every deployment posted `“process”` as its process key instead of the model’s actual id, and sub-process lookups by `calledElement` never matched.

A new `findProcessElement` helper uses `getElementsByTagNameNS` to match on local name across namespaces, and all four call sites route through it. The test covering this had asserted the fallback as correct, attributing it to a jsdom quirk — that reading was half right: the fixture behind it declared none of the prefixes it used, so `DOMParser` rejected the document outright and returned a `<parsererror>` in which nothing was findable under any lookup, masking the real defect underneath.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Error overlay was unreachable from the view that raised it
details: The overlay lived inside `App`’s right panel, which is hidden whenever `viewMode` is Orchestration, BPMN, Form, Document, ROPA, DSO or either validator. `handleRefreshCache` can only be triggered from Orchestration, so a failed cache clear set the error state correctly and then had nowhere to render — silent until the user happened to navigate elsewhere, where a stale error appeared out of context.

The overlay is now a direct child of the workspace container, which is already positioned relative, so it renders in every view. `App.test.tsx` previously asserted the broken behaviour explicitly; it now asserts the error appears on the view that caused it and is dismissible there.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Every deploy now gated on lint and the test suite
details: None of the six Azure workflows ran a test step, blocking or otherwise. That was a deliberate P7 decision taken when backend coverage was first measured at 13.82% statements — gating on a number that low would have been theatre — recorded as conditional on backend breadth improving. v2026.08.2 took the backend from 16.79% to 98.06%, meeting the condition.

The backend workflows already installed and linted, so the test step slots in beside the existing `npm run lint`. The frontend workflows had no npm steps at all, because the Static Web Apps action builds inside its own container and runs none of this repository’s scripts; they gain an explicit install, lint and test sequence ahead of the deploy action. The two `ropa-site` workflows are deliberately untouched — that package is a static `index.html` with no build and no test script to run.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Repo-side test documentation retired in favour of the documentation site
details: Deletes `docs/TESTS.md` (982 lines) and `docs/TESTING-GUIDE.md` (228 lines). The IOU Architecture documentation site is now the single source of truth for test documentation, at `linked-data-explorer/developer/testing`; the repo-side copies had drifted from what the suites actually do and are not maintained.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: lint-staged skipped backend files at pre-commit
details: Companion to the `check-format` fix below — the same blind spot, one stage earlier. `lint-staged` was configured with a single glob for `packages/frontend/**`, so committing a backend file ran neither Prettier nor ESLint over it.

Adds `packages/backend/src/**/*.ts` with the backend’s own `eslint.config.js`. The scope is deliberately `src/**/*.ts` rather than the whole package: that is exactly what the backend’s `check-format` gates, so pre-commit and pre-push now agree rather than one rewriting files the other never checks.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Root check-format silently skipped the backend
details: The two workspaces named their Prettier check differently — backend `format:check`, frontend `check-format` — while the root script runs `npm run check-format --workspaces --if-present`. Because `--if-present` skips a missing script rather than failing, the backend was quietly dropped from every root `check-format` run.

`.husky/pre-push` runs exactly that root script, so backend formatting was never actually gated on push. The gap was silent in both directions: the root command exited 0, and its output listed only the frontend. The backend now defines `check-format` as its canonical name, with `format:check` retained as an alias.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: "years and months duration(...)" built-in name false-flagged as an unresolved variable (INT-007)
details: FEEL_RESERVED had the singular year/month/day/hour/minute/second (for year(...)/month(...) single-word built-ins) but not the plural years/months -- the two words of the "years and months duration(...)" built-in's own name. Its leading words aren't preceded by a dot, so only the reserved-word check catches them; the pre-existing dot-check already handled the trailing .years/.months property access on the duration result correctly.

Reproduced live against HvA_full_dmn_export-patched.dmn: 12 INT-007 warnings across 6 decisions, all false positives from this exact construct (e.g. "(years and months duration(npGeboortedatum, peildatum)).years").

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: POST /v1/dmns/evaluate/:decisionKey -- raw passthrough evaluate proxy
details: The CPSV Editor's DMN tab called Operaton's evaluate endpoint directly from the browser, which CORS blocks for a local dev origin. This route proxies the call server-side instead, forwarding Operaton's response byte-for-byte and status-for-status (success array or exception object) rather than the usual {success, data, error} envelope, since the DMN tab reads Operaton's raw JSON directly.

New evaluateRaw() on operatonService passes variables straight through, without the plain-JS-value type inference evaluateDecision() does for its own (different) caller contract -- the DMN tab already constructs Operaton-shaped request bodies itself, so re-wrapping them would double-wrap and break the request.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: POST /v1/dmns/deploy -- ad-hoc raw DMN XML deploy
details: Deploys DMN content directly, without requiring pre-registered LDE norm identifiers first -- built for the CPSV Editor's DMN tab, which has an uploaded/generated DMN file with no registry entry of its own. A thin wrapper around the already-proven operatonService.deployDrd(), routing the CPSV Editor's own Deploy button through this backend instead of calling Operaton directly from the browser -- same CORS reasoning as the evaluate proxy above.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: dmn-validation.service.ts EXEC-* checks were all dead code
details: cprmvAttr()'s primary namespace-aware lookup called el.attr({ name, ns }) -- libxmljs2's setter overload, not a getter: it creates/sets an attribute and returns the element itself for chaining, which has no .value(). The throw was silently swallowed by the function's own catch, so EXEC-002 through EXEC-010 -- every rule-level and decision-level CPRMV validation check this service had ever shipped -- never actually fired, for any DMN, since the file was written. Fixed by dropping the broken setter-form branch and reading attributes via a direct attrs() scan.

Also fixed: CPRMV_NS was hardcoded to the legacy cprmv.open-regels.nl/0.3.0/ namespace, so a DMN using the current standaarden.open-regels.nl/standards/cprmv/0.4.1# namespace would short-circuit on an EXEC-001 "CPRMV not declared" before reaching any check -- CPRMV_NAMESPACES now accepts both.
New EXEC-011/EXEC-012 checks validate cell-level dct:source/cprmv:isBasedOn format on grounded DMN cells; EXEC-013 closes a pre-existing gap where cprmv:extends' format was never checked at all.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Bump seed versions so shellId reaches existing users' example sub-processes
details: example_tree_felling, example_zorgtoeslag_provisional, and example_zorgtoeslag_final's seed data got shellId added in an earlier commit, but their EXAMPLE_VERSIONS entries weren't bumped, so seed() skipped re-saving them for existing users -- both localStorage and Postgres kept the shellId-less copy, which falls back to the old ambiguous bpmnProcessId match and renders under every shell sharing that id.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: E2E badge color changed from indigo to orange
details: Indigo read too close to EXAMPLE's blue in practice. Orange is clearly distinct from every other badge color in use (blue/amber/green/violet/teal).

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Persist shellId and e2e status through Postgres, not just localStorage
details: Both bugs traced to the same cause: hydrateFromServer() treats the Postgres-backed server list as authoritative and replaces local state with it on every BpmnModeler mount. The two fields added for the e2e-fixtures work in the previous two commits never reached the database, so they didn't survive that replace.

process_definitions.status had CHECK (status IN ('example', 'wip')) -- no 'e2e'. Saving an e2e-status BPMN process violated the constraint and the save failed silently (fetch() doesn't reject on non-2xx responses). shellId was never part of the DB schema, upsert, or list query, so every hydrate overwrote the local, correctly-classified copy with the server's shellId-less one -- the shell/subprocess duplication fix from the previous two commits never actually held past the first render.
Adds shell_id to process_definitions (additive, idempotent) and widens the status CHECK to include 'e2e'. Threads shellId through the mapper, upsert, list query, and the frontend's save request.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Disambiguate shell/subprocess matching by shellId, not just bpmnProcessId
details: Shell/subprocess matching keyed purely on calledElement === shell.bpmnProcessId, a string that's no longer unique once a shell is deliberately duplicated -- an e2e-fixtures copy of a seeded example shell intentionally keeps the same bpmnProcessId, since that's the real production Operaton key. ProcessList's catalog grouping rendered every subprocess under *every* shell sharing its bpmnProcessId instead of just its own.

Adds shellId (holding the parent shell's own local record id) alongside the existing calledElement; grouping and BpmnModeler's language/organization propagation now prefer shellId when present, falling back to the old match for records saved before this field existed. Also wires E2E badge detection for imported BPMN processes off the existing e2e-fixtures textAnnotation marker.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: E2E status badge for imported e2e-fixtures forms and documents
details: Imported e2e-fixtures files rendered as generic WIP/DRAFT, indistinguishable from arbitrary in-progress work. Adds a new 'e2e' status, detected at import time from a self-describing marker baked into each fixture file: a wrapper key on forms (stripped before handing the schema to form-js) and the fixture's own status field on documents.
Extracts a shared StatusBadge component used by ProcessList, FormList and DocumentList, replacing three near-identical inline badge blocks and adding the new E2E badge to all three in one place.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Normalise line endings to LF via .gitattributes
details: The backend's .prettierrc sets endOfLine: lf, but the repo had no .gitattributes, so a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true produced CRLF working files and npm run format:check failed on already-correctly-formatted content -- a loop no commit could fix, since Git kept renormalising files straight back to CRLF. Forcing LF in the working tree closes the loop; batch files stay pinned to CRLF and images are marked binary.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Make CPRMV attribute rules actually fire (cprmvAttr namespaced lookup was broken)
details: cprmvAttr() tried el.attr({ name, ns: CPRMV_NS }) before falling back to a scan of el.attrs(). In libxmljs2 0.37 that object form is not a namespaced lookup: it sets attributes literally called "name" and "ns" on the element and returns a value with no .value() method, so the call threw. The function's own try/catch swallowed the throw and returned null, so the working attrs() fallback beneath it was never reached -- EXEC-002..EXEC-010 and CON-001..CON-003 never fired for any input, so ten validation rules were dead while reporting a clean result, and every inspected element was mutated with two junk attributes.

Dropping the object-form fast path is the whole fix. Verified against all 16 tracked .dmn files: no newly-reported issues, since none carried cprmv:* attributes at the time -- the rules now work for RONL DMN+ files that do.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Raise backend statement coverage from 17% to 98%
details: Adds 31 test files covering every previously-untested backend module and extends 3 existing ones. No production code changed. Statements 16.79% -> 98.06%, branches 18.10% -> 89.18%, tests 118 -> 1078 across 48 suites.

Previously at 0%: all 11 untested route modules, routes/index and routes/registry, 8 untested services, db/pool, db/migrate, utils/logger and utils/rootViews. Module-level singletons (db/pool, utils/logger, utils/config) are re-imported per test case via jest.isolateModules with a patched environment; @rdfjs/dataset and rdf-validate-shacl (ESM-only) are stubbed so the SHACL suite exercises layer loading and issue mapping rather than the RDF libraries themselves.

Documented (not fixed here, as a testing-scope decision) the cprmvAttr() defect fixed two commits later in this release: calling el.attr({ name, ns }) throws in libxmljs2 0.37 instead of performing a namespaced lookup, leaving ten validation rules permanently inert.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Fix an E2E fixture's BPMN schema error
details: Operaton's BPMN parser rejected TreeFellingPermitSubProcessE2E.bpmn (ENGINE-09005, a businessRuleTask found where an artifact-group element was expected) because the fixture-warning textAnnotation/association pair immediately preceded the file's first businessRuleTask. Every other fixture with the same annotation pattern has a scriptTask in that position instead, which validates fine, so this specific adjacency had never been submitted to Operaton for real parsing before. Fixed by moving the annotation to the end of the process body — after all flow elements, before the closing tag — which is also the more conventional placement for BPMN artifacts.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Give e2e-fixtures sub-processes their own Operaton keys
details: TreeFellingPermitSubProcess and ZorgtoeslagProvisionalSubProcess renamed to TreeFellingPermitSubProcessE2E / ZorgtoeslagProvisionalSubProcessE2E (filename, bpmn:process id, and the calling shell's callActivity calledElement). Prevents LDE's own process catalog from conflating the e2e-fixtures copy with the seeded-examples copy of the same sub-process — both previously shared the same bpmn:process id, so importing/redeploying the fixture could silently reuse the example's stale content instead. Shells (AwbShellProcess, AwbZorgtoeslagProcess) and RipR21Process are unaffected.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Resolve shared DMN decisions as untenanted from tenant-scoped business-rule-tasks
details: Confirmed empirically against a live Operaton instance: by default, a business-rule-task's camunda:decisionRef resolves against a decision definition under the exact same tenant-id as the calling process instance, with no fallback to a shared, untenanted decision even when one exists. camunda:decisionRefTenantId can override this, but only as an EL expression evaluating to null (${null}) — a literal empty string is silently ignored. Applied to all 7 business-rule-tasks across the 4 fixture BPMNs that reference genuinely tenant-agnostic, shared regulatory-logic DMN tables, so they keep resolving correctly now that the calling processes themselves carry a real tenant-id.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Fix a copy-paste processKey bug and nest sub-process fixtures under their shell
details: ZORGTOESLAG_PROVISIONAL_BESCHIKKING's processKey read 'AwbShellProcess' — copy-pasted from the tree-felling document template above it — corrected to 'AwbZorgtoeslagProcess', the process it actually belongs to; the regenerated .document fixture matches the corrected source exactly.

AwbShellProcess calls TreeFellingPermitSubProcess and AwbZorgtoeslagProcess calls ZorgtoeslagProvisionalSubProcess via a BPMN callActivity, which BpmnModeler.tsx auto-detects and bundles into a single deployment call — the manifest now nests each sub-process's fixture entry under its shell's own subProcesses array instead of listing it as a flat sibling, with a new test asserting each shell's BPMN genuinely contains a calledElement matching its declared nested sub-process keys.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Assemble the e2e-fixtures test bundle
details: A new, dedicated e2e-fixtures/<tenant>/ directory with a manifest.json and an integrity test, replacing two pre-existing, already-diverged 'examples' locations (broad stale reference material, and the general-purpose seeded-example store used by the BPMN Modeler's load-example buttons) as the single source of truth for ronl-business-api's E2E test suite. AwbShellProcess, TreeFellingPermitSubProcess, and AwbZorgtoeslagProcess/ZorgtoeslagProvisionalSubProcess are seeded from the proven-freshest examples copy; RipR21Process is assembled by merging two divergent draft folders (a swimlane redesign missing several of its own form files, filled in from an older, complete draft) and renamed from RipPhase1Process. Also adds the two decision-document fixtures (example_treefelling_beschikking, example_zorgtoeslag_provisional_beschikking) that both seeded BPMNs reference but had no corresponding .document file for anywhere in the repo, converted from their DocumentTemplate source objects.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Make organization mandatory when deploying a BPMN process
details: The BPMN Modeler's Deploy action now requires an Organization value before it will submit a deployment, sent to Operaton as its native tenant-id (POST /deployment/create's tenant-id field) — closing the gap where a process could be deployed with no tenant-id at all, invisible to any tenant-scoped lookup an application later needs to make against it.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Spec: mandatory organization/tenantId at BPMN deploy time
details: Design doc for making organization mandatory at deploy time and sending it to Operaton as native tenant-id, the foundation this release's e2e-fixtures work and ronl-business-api's own tenant-mandatory adoption both build on.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Add Ede and Gelderland to DSO Viewer location presets
details: Extends the DSO Viewer's activities-tab LOCATION_PRESETS with the municipality of Ede and the province of Gelderland, alongside the existing Lelystad and Flevoland entries. This one array drives both the location filter buttons and the authority-name lookup used when importing forms, so no other code changes were needed.

OINs were sourced from overheid.nl's Identificatiecodes records for each organization and cross-checked structurally: each OIN embeds the org's own RSIN, and both new values follow the same 00000001<RSIN>000 pattern as the existing Lelystad/Flevoland entries.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: DMN validator misses id-attribute deploy failures, false-positives on multi-word FEEL names
details: Adds BIZ-010 through BIZ-014, flagging <input>/<output>/<rule>/<inputEntry>/<outputEntry> elements missing the id attribute as errors. Operaton's DMN transformer requires id on these decision-table clause elements even though the DMN 1.3 XSD marks it optional, and rejects such files with DMN-02011 at deploy time — a class of failure this validator previously reported as fully valid.

Fixes two false-positive sources in INT-007. FEEL names may legally contain spaces, and a bare <inputExpression> that is itself one multi-word declared name (e.g. "natuurlijke persoon.woonachtig in de gemeente waar wordt aangevraagd") was being shredded word-by-word by the identifier tokenizer, with every word flagged as an unresolved variable; a whole-string match against declared/produced names is now tried first, before falling back to tokenization. Separately, FEEL_RESERVED was missing the single-word FEEL date/time component functions (year, month, day, hour, minute, second) alongside the already-excluded date/time/duration/number/string built-ins, so year(...) calls were flagging "year" itself as unresolved.

Found while debugging amsterdam/individuele-inkomenstoeslag-iknow.dmn's Operaton deploy failure in the CPSV Editor (ttl-editor) repo — together these fixes reduced that file's Interaction Rules warnings from 83 to 12. The residual 12 (multi-word names embedded inside compound expressions rather than as bare references, plus one likely real DRD-wiring gap in the source DMN) are documented as open issues rather than fixed, since closing them properly needs a materially larger longest-match tokenizer change.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: P7 — coverage report + CI-wiring deferral decision
details: Closes out the testing plan with a real --coverage run across both packages: 109 backend tests but only 13.82% backend statement coverage (the tested files are near-100%, but large route/service files — dmn.routes.ts, operaton.service.ts, sparql.service.ts, dmn-validation.service.ts, dso.service.ts and others — remain entirely untested), against 557 frontend tests at 74.03% statement coverage across 59 files, where P4–P6 reached every component/page/service directory at least once.

Decision: no CI test step is added to the Azure workflows yet, blocking or non-blocking — the same call ronl-business-api made at 83.39% coverage with its full P1–P11 backlog done, applied here specifically because the backend gap is breadth (whole files never touched) rather than depth (dense sub-branches in already-tested files). Documented in TESTING-GUIDE.md's new "CI roadmap (P7)" section, with the condition for revisiting it: once backend breadth improves, or the team decides breadth alone is an acceptable bar to gate on.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.8 — App.tsx + Changelog.tsx integration coverage (P6 complete)
details: Adds 31 tests across the final P6 phase — the top-level integration components that route between everything else. App.tsx (838 lines) renders 12 feature components plus executeSparqlQuery, all mocked as clickable/inspectable stubs, isolating the orchestrator's own state machine: sidebar navigation across all 12 views, localStorage viewMode persistence (with fallback on an invalid stored value), the always-mounted-but-CSS-hidden DmnValidator/ShaclValidator panes, the SPARQL run/error/auto-visualize-on-?s-?p-?o flow, the sample-query library, the settings panel (endpoint add/delete/reset, the DSO pre/prod toggle persisting to its own localStorage key), Orchestration-view cache refresh, and CSV export.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.7 — DocumentComposer component coverage (tiptap + dnd-kit phase)

sections.title: Query library — rules and concepts now resolve for CPRMV 0.4.1 datasets
items: The 'Rules with Their Services', 'Count Rules per Service' and 'Services with All Their Rules (Detailed)' queries joined ?rule cpsv:implements ?service directly. Since the CPSV-AP RuleShape change a cpsv:Rule's cpsv:implements points at an eli:LegalResource (the resource the service declares via cv:hasLegalResource), so datasets published in the newer shape (e.g. the Flevoland Thuisbatterij service) returned no rules. The queries now UNION over both link paths — the direct edge and the shared legal resource — and read validFrom/confidence from cprmv041: (was ronl:, a predicate the data never carried).

The 'NL-SBB Concepts and Services' query broke at the variable→DMN hop: a concept's dct:subject points at a bare DMN variable URI (<dmnUri>/input/N or /output/N) that newer exports emit without a cpsv:isRequiredBy / cpsv:produces edge, so the concept could not reach its DMN or service. It now keeps the explicit edge for older data and, when absent, derives the DMN URI from the variable URI (OPTIONAL edges + COALESCE with an IRI(REPLACE(...)) fallback), then matches cprmv:implements or cprmv041:implements.

Auto-generated DMN decision rules ('Decision rule <id>' placeholder titles) are filtered out of the rule listings, and SELECT DISTINCT de-duplicates. For the Thuisbatterij dataset this surfaces its 3 business rules (was hidden) and 21 concepts, and drops ~60 placeholder rows across the catalogue.

sections.title: Fix boardOwner injection breaking BPMN deploys with a process documentation element
items: Deploying a process whose <bpmn:process> element carries a <bpmn:documentation> child (e.g. ThuisbatterijSubsidieAanvraagProcess) always failed with a bare "Request failed with status code 400", because the deploy-time boardOwner tagging spliced its <extensionElements> block in directly after the opening <process> tag — ahead of the existing documentation element. The BPMN/XSD schema requires documentation to precede extensionElements, so Operaton's schema validator rejected the resulting XML (ENGINE-09005 ParseException).

injectBoardOwner now skips past any leading <documentation> element(s) before inserting or locating extensionElements, preserving valid schema order. Deploys with a documented process now succeed identically to undocumented ones.

Deploy failures now surface Operaton's real error: the deployment service captures and logs the response body (operatonResponse/operatonStatus) instead of just the generic Axios message, and getErrorDetails() checks isAxiosError before the generic Error branch — previously dead code, since AxiosError extends Error and always matched the generic branch first, silently discarding response.data.

sections.title: /v1/norms — ?cprmv_version= selector (0.3.0 / 0.3.2 / 0.4.1)
items: A new ?cprmv_version= query parameter on /v1/norms selects which CPRMV vocabulary version to query and emit — one of 0.3.0, 0.3.2 or 0.4.1 (else 400), defaulting to 0.3.0. The query was previously hardcoded to 0.3.0, so anything published under another namespace returned nothing.

All three versions carry flat cprmv:Rule resources with the same predicates (id, definition, rulesetId, ruleIdPath, situatie, norm), so the rules query is one shape with the namespace swapped: 0.3.0/0.3.2 use the cprmv.open-regels versioned-path IRI, 0.4.1 the standaarden.open-regels 0.4.1# IRI. The selected version is threaded through the rules query, the publish-format output keys, the cprmv_version envelope and the ETag/cache signature, so versions never share a cache entry.

Per-ruleset metadata (dataset_versions) differs by version: 0.3.x reads cprmv:Dataset (dct:issued + dcat:version), while 0.4.1 has no cprmv:Dataset and reads cprmv:RuleSet (cprmv:validFrom, which doubles as the ETag / Last-Modified freshness signal since 0.4.1 has no dct:issued). Verified against live data: 0.4.1 returns 72 norms across 7 rulesets, with cache headers and the 0.3.x paths unchanged.

sections.title: Process board ownership — deploy-time tagging
items: Deploy modal now requires a board owner: a new "Board ownership" section auto-detects the board from the process's candidate groups (infra/rip → Infra-board, caseworker/hr → Caseworker) and lets you override it. Deploy is blocked until a board is resolved.

Deployed BPMN is stamped with a process-level camunda:property boardOwner (explicit choice or auto-derived). Injection is idempotent and non-destructive — on any unexpected BPMN shape the original XML is deployed untouched.

boardOwner is persisted on the process_definitions record (new board_owner column) and exposed via /bundles/public, so downstream consumers (ronl-business-api Procesbibliotheek and archive split) can read it.

sections.title: RIP Phase 1 — derive portfolio leadRole
items: The Map role outputs script now sets a leadRole process variable, derived from the intake projectType (contractbeheer → manager-pb, otherwise projectleider). This is the ownership signal the Infra-board Portfolio ROL filter reads.

Distinct from the task candidateGroups: leadRole names who owns the project in the portfolio, not who can claim its tasks. Takes effect for instances started after redeploy; the projectType → leadRole mapping is a placeholder to confirm with the business.

sections.title: CPRMV SHACL — ParameterWaardeShape and TemporalRuleShape
items: Added cprmv:ParameterWaardeShape targeting cprmv:ParameterWaarde: skos:notation [1,1] xsd:string and skos:prefLabel [1,n] rdf:langString are mandatory; schema:value [0,1] xsd:decimal, schema:unitCode [0,1] xsd:string, dct:description [0,1] rdf:langString, and cprmv:validFrom/validUntil [0,1] xsd:date are optional. Previously cprmv:ParameterWaarde had no SHACL shape at all, so the entire Parameters section of an editor-generated TTL was unvalidated.

Added cprmv:TemporalRuleShape targeting cprmv:TemporalRule: cprmv:validFrom [0,1] xsd:date, cprmv:validUntil [0,1] xsd:date, cprmv:confidenceLevel [0,1] xsd:string, and cprmv:isBasedOn [0,n] sh:class cpsv:Rule — all optional. Previously the temporal extensions on cpsv:Rule (validity window, confidence level, extends) were unvalidated by any SHACL shape.
Also adds skos:, schema:, and dct: @prefix declarations required by the new shapes; no changes to existing shapes in the file.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: SHACL Validator: long issue messages and focus-node locations were cut off with an ellipsis and could not be read — the location used a single-line CSS truncate. Messages and locations now wrap in full (break-words / break-all) and expose the complete text on hover (title tooltip).

SHACL backend: removed the 60-character cap on offending values reported for cardinality (maxCount / uniqueLang) violations, so the full value appears in the issue message instead of being truncated with an ellipsis.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: DMNs published under the new CPRMV 0.4.1 namespace (e.g. vast_bedrag_op_vestiging) were missing from /v1/dmns and the ChainBuilder DMN picker — getAllDmns and the chain-link queries only matched cprmv:DecisionModel under the old 0.3.0 namespace. Both namespaces are now supported side by side until existing 0.3.0 data is migrated.

Fixed 'Fill with test data' in the ChainBuilder input form not visibly filling Integer/Double fields when the RDF-sourced test value is 0 — the input rendered as empty (0 || '' = '') instead of showing 0.

sections.title: DSO Integration — deploy-ready DMN + form badge
items: Extracted DSO DMNs now carry camunda:historyTimeToLive, so they deploy to Operaton exactly as handed off — the consumer no longer has to patch the DMN before deploying. LDE now produces a fully deploy-ready and evaluatable DMN (DMN 1.3, input ids, FEEL-safe variable names, output typeRefs, history TTL).
Forms imported from DSO now show a green DSO badge in the Form Editor list, instead of the generic yellow WIP badge.

sections.title: SHACL Validator — CPRMV layer + validation test fixtures
items: The SHACL validator now checks uploaded Turtle against a CPRMV 0.4.1 shape layer alongside CPSV-AP 3.2.0 and the RONL Custom rules; the results panel renders the new layer automatically.

Added valid/invalid test fixtures for every layer — CPRMV (cprmv-conformant.ttl / cprmv-nonconformant.ttl), CPSV-AP (cpsv-ap-conformant.ttl / cpsv-ap-rule-nonconformant.ttl), and RONL (rule- and org-collision pass/fail) — plus a malformed-Turtle case covering the parser path.

sections.title: DSO Integration — Phase 2d + 4.2
items: Activities tab now supports name search: fixing a location (Lelystad / Flevoland) loads that authority's full activity set in one call and reveals a search box that live-filters by name, so activities like 'Boom kappen of houtopstand vellen' are findable without walking the hierarchy.

↓ Import into LDE button (Indieningsvereisten only) saves the generated form-js scaffold straight into the Form Editor as a draft, named after the activity and tagged with the authority — no manual download/import step needed.
Imported forms are now tagged with the readable authority name (e.g. 'Lelystad') instead of the bare RTR code (GM0995), falling back to the code for authorities outside the known presets.

sections.title: DSO Integration — DMN publish handoff (Phase 4.1)
items: Publish via CPSV Editor button (Conclusie only) opens the CPSV Editor with a deep-link to publish the extracted DMN to TriplyDB, where the LDE DMN picker can consume it — no local DMN store needed.

Extracted DMNs are now normalized to deploy and evaluate on Operaton: DMN 1.2 is upgraded to 1.3, missing input ids are added, variable names are made FEEL-safe (hyphens/spaces broke evaluation), and output columns get an explicit typeRef.
Verified end-to-end against Operaton: the normalized HoutopstandVellen decision deploys (all 7 decisions) and the root decision evaluates without the previous FEEL error.

sections.title: DSO Integration — Phase 2a + 4
items: Activity Detail panel now shows an 'Applicable Rules' section listing toepasbare regels fetched live from the DSO Uitvoeren Gegevens API, grouped by rule type (Conclusie / Indieningsvereisten) with validity date and STTR version.
↓ STTR button downloads the raw STTR XML for any rule type.
↓ Extract DMN button (Conclusie only) extracts the embedded DMN decision table as a standalone .dmn file ready for import into LDE or deployment to Operaton.

↓ Form scaffold button (Indieningsvereisten only) generates a form-js JSON scaffold from the STTR questionnaire, mapping boolean questions to checkboxes, list questions to select fields with options, number questions to number fields, and attachment requirements to labelled textfields.
Added ronl:dsoActiviteitUrn extension on TreeFellingPermitSubProcess linking it to nl.imow-gm0995.activiteit.HoutopstandVellen (Gemeente Lelystad).

sections.title: BPMN Modeler
items: Uploaded BPMN processes that form a shell/subprocess pair are now automatically linked: a process with call-activity elements is classified as a shell, and any process whose BPMN process ID is targeted by a shell's call-activity is classified as its subprocess. The relationship is detected both on fresh imports and retroactively on startup, so previously uploaded standalone processes are reclassified without requiring a re-upload.
Removed two unused TypeScript imports (DsoWerkzaamheid, zoekActiviteiten) in DsoExplorer.

sections.title: SHACL Validator
items: Vendored the canonical CPSV-AP 3.2.0 SHACL shapes (SEMIC) — the CPSV-AP layer is now active, validating the full model (PublicService, Rule, PublicOrganisation, ContactPoint, Channel, Address, …) across 32 shapes. Previously this layer reported no shapes.
Collapsed the earlier CPSV-AP Core and CPSV-AP Vocabularies layers into a single CPSV-AP 3.2.0 layer, matching SEMIC's combined shape file for the 3.2.0 release.
Layer results now distinguish 'Not loaded' (no shapes present for that layer) from 'OK' (evaluated and clean), so an unvendored layer no longer shows a misleading green check.
Offending values listed in cardinality and uniqueLang messages are now whitespace-normalised and capped at 60 characters, keeping long published descriptions readable.
Added a fully CPSV-AP-conformant example plus deterministic merge-simulated test coverage (a cross-publication homepage collision), alongside the existing file-local fixtures.

sections.title: SHACL Validator
items: New SHACL Validator view in the sidebar: drop one or more CPSV-AP Turtle (.ttl) files and validate them against the bundled CPSV-AP 3.2.0 and RONL SHACL shapes before publishing. Results reuse the DMN Validator's layered layout, grouped into CPSV-AP Core, CPSV-AP Vocabularies, and RONL Custom with per-layer error/warning/info counts.

Two backend endpoints under a new Validation route category: POST /v1/shacl/validate (file-local) and POST /v1/shacl/validate-merged. Both return the same { valid, parseError, layers, summary } shape as /v1/dmns/validate, so the frontend renders them with the existing components.

Merge-simulated mode unions the uploaded file with the triples already published for its subjects — fetched from the configured SPARQL endpoint via a standard SPARQL 1.1 CONSTRUCT with one level of blank-node closure — then validates the union. This catches fan-out against live data that a file-local check cannot see; an optional endpoint field overrides the server default.

RONL shape PublicOrganisationUniquenessShape: at most one foaf:homepage, dct:identifier and cv:spatial per cv:PublicOrganisation, plus sh:uniqueLang on skos:prefLabel. Flags the duplicate-homepage fan-out where one organisation URI ends up with both a www. and non-www. homepage across publications.

RONL shape RuleUniquenessShape: sh:uniqueLang on dct:title and dct:description for cpsv:Rule. Detects subject-URI collisions where several distinct rules were authored under one URI and merge into N titles × M descriptions of duplicate rows in SPARQL results, while tolerating legitimate bilingual (nl/en) labels.
Cardinality and uniqueLang violations list the offending values inline (whitespace-normalised and capped at 60 characters) so collisions are immediately identifiable.

sections.title: New Features
items: Download the deployed DMN XML directly from Operaton via the new GET /v1/dmns/:identifier/xml endpoint — the file is streamed as <identifier>.dmn with the correct Content-Type and Content-Disposition headers so browsers save it automatically.
DMN list and detail responses now include an xmlUrl field pointing to the new download endpoint, making the link self-discoverable for API clients without prior knowledge of the URL pattern.
Backward compatible: the legacy GET /api/dmns/:definitionKey/xml route remains available for existing consumers.

sections.title: DMN validator: INT-007 false positives eliminated
items: INT-007 (Interaction Rules layer) no longer flags valid intra-DRD references. An <inputExpression> may legitimately reference a value produced by another decision wired in via <informationRequirement><requiredDecision> — that name is the producing decision's <variable name> or <decisionTable>/<output name>, never an <inputData>. The rule now resolves requiredDecision targets and treats their output variables as satisfied, mirroring the requiredInput → inputData resolution INT-001 already performs.

INT-007 now parses FEEL expressions instead of whole-text matching. Previously the entire <inputExpression><text> was treated as one variable name, so date and time(aanvraagDatum) demanded an <inputData name="date and time(aanvraagDatum)"> and any operator expression false-fired. A new shared extractFeelIdentifiers() helper strips string literals, unwraps built-in calls (date(...), date and time(...), number(...), string(...), not(...), …), drops FEEL keywords/operators and qualified-name/property segments after a dot, and extracts each referenced identifier — every identifier is checked individually.

Decision outputs are excluded from the input-contract check entirely. Output variable names (decision <variable> and decision-table <output name>) are, by construction, never external inputs and are no longer subject to the must-have-matching-inputData requirement.

Genuine gaps still flagged: an inputExpression identifier that resolves to neither a declared <inputData> nor a requiredDecision-produced output continues to raise INT-007, now naming the specific identifier rather than the raw expression string.

Verified against real DMNs that deploy and evaluate correctly on Operaton: RONL_Heusden_Heusdenpas.dmn (aanmerkingHeusdenPas consumed purely via requiredDecision), RONL_SVB_Leeftijden.dmn (date(dagVanAanvraag).year property access), EmployeeRoleAssignment.dmn, tree-felling-decision.dmn and replacement-tree-decision.dmn all validate clean; backend tsc --noEmit passes.
No API or response-shape change. POST /v1/dmns/validate is unchanged; only the interaction-layer issue set for affected files differs (fewer false-positive warnings).

sections.title: Concurrent applicable periods per ruleset on /v1/norms
items: A single BWB ruleset can have multiple cprmv:Dataset records — different applicable periods of the same law (e.g. the 2025-01-01 and 2026-01-01 editions of the Participatiewet) are concurrent and equally authoritative, not competing versions. The v1.7 design hid all but the latest; v1.8 surfaces them all.

Breaking shape change: dataset_versions[<rulesetid>] is now a list of { version, published_at, title } records, not a single object. Replaces v1.7.0 (which was never used externally — API stability contract hadn't been promised at that release).
List is pre-sorted: version descending with nulls at the end, ties broken by published_at descending. Element [0] is the most-recent applicable version of that ruleset.
SPARQL query simplified: dropped the FILTER NOT EXISTS subpattern and now fetches all cprmv:Dataset records. Grouping and sort live in the service layer.

sections.title: Cache header semantics preserved across the shape change
items: ETag now hashes every (version, published_at) pair in dataset_versions — a new applicable period being added to any ruleset changes the ETag
Last-Modified is max(published_at) across all records in the response (not just the first per ruleset)
Cache-Control semantics unchanged: full headers when every rulesetid has metadata; no-cache otherwise

sections.title: Graph-name traceability on /v1/triplydb/update-service
items: New optional graphName field in the POST /v1/triplydb/update-service request body — accepts the IRI of the graph that triggered the sync (e.g. https://regels.overheid.nl/graphs/Sociale_Verzekeringsbank/aow-leeftijd); requests that omit it continue to work unchanged

graphName threaded through to the route logger as graphName and to the service logger as triggeredByGraph — multi-publish flows landing in distinct per-service graphs are now traceable end-to-end without inspecting TriplyDB internals

updateService() in packages/backend/src/services/triplydb.service.ts extended with a fourth optional parameter graphName?: string; existing graphNames?: string[] parameter unchanged for backward compatibility
Response envelope from /v1/triplydb/update-service now echoes graphName when it was supplied in the request, omitted otherwise — additive shape change with no breaking impact on existing clients

The underlying TriplyDB sync call (POST /datasets/{account}/{dataset}/services/{serviceName} with body {"sync":"true"}) is unchanged — graphName is purely observability metadata, since the TriplyDB sync endpoint has no graph-scoping mechanism of its own

sections.title: Per-rulesetid dataset versioning on /v1/norms
items: New envelope field: dataset_versions — a per-rulesetid map keyed by cprmv:rulesetId, each entry carrying { version, published_at } for the latest cprmv:Dataset record of that ruleset

Each BWB ruleset (BWBR0002471, BWBR0004044, ...) is published as a distinct cprmv:Dataset resource in TriplyDB, on its own publication cadence; a single /v1/norms response can span multiple rulesets at different versions
Backend picks the latest cprmv:Dataset per cprmv:rulesetId via a FILTER NOT EXISTS subpattern — historical versions remain queryable in TriplyDB but consumers see only the latest
New envelope field: cprmv_version — backend constant extracted from the CPRMV namespace URI, describes which vocabulary the backend speaks independently of which data is published
Internal 60-second cache on the dataset metadata SPARQL query — biannual data tolerates this happily and keeps the metadata lookup off the hot path

sections.title: HTTP cache headers for G2G consumers
items: ETag header: opaque 8-hex strong validator hashed over the sorted dataset_versions map plus all request parameters affecting the response shape

Last-Modified header: max(published_at) across the response's datasets in RFC 7231 format — If-Modified-Since returns 304 only when nothing in the consumer's query has been republished since their last fetch
Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 set only when every rulesetid in the response has dataset metadata; falls back to no-cache otherwise

Safe-by-default partial-coverage policy: if any rulesetid in the response is missing a cprmv:Dataset record, all three cache headers degrade to no-cache so consumers can't be misled into serving stale data for an unversioned ruleset
Single-rulesetid queries get a fast 304 path: the cheap (cached) metadata lookup decides freshness BEFORE the expensive rules SPARQL query runs
New utility module packages/backend/src/utils/etag.ts with computeNormsEtag() and computeLastModified(): key-order-independent and undefined-tolerant serialisation

sections.title: API stability contract published
items: New IOU documentation page at /linked-data-explorer/reference/api-stability — binding contract for G2G consumers covering the four versioning layers, PK semantics, additive evolution promise, per-rulesetid publication detection, partial-coverage behaviour, breaking-change criteria, and 24-month deprecation policy when v2 eventually arrives
Documents the immutability guarantee for the (rulesetid, applicable_date, rulesetid_index) tuple as the eternal primary key — consumers can cache permanently and never invalidate
Documents the rule_id_path_key field as the logical identifier for querying 'the current value of this rule' across its lifetime
Documents the cprmv:Dataset publication model: each BWB ruleset is a distinct dataset on its own cadence; rollout is from scratch with no retroactive backfill of existing rulesets
Quick-reference table at the bottom covering the questions a new G2G consumer is most likely to ask first

sections.title: Stable keys and version indices on /v1/norms
items: New rule_id_path_key field: rule_id_path with the date and index segments removed, e.g. "BWBR0002471_2025-01-01_0, Artikel 2, lid 6" → "BWBR0002471, Artikel 2, lid 6"; stable across versions of the same ruleset, suitable as a deduplication key when aggregating norms across applicable_date values
New rulesetid_index field: the integer index segment after the date in rule_id_path (e.g. the _0 in BWBR..._2025-01-01_0); distinguishes multiple versions published on the same date

Both new fields, together with applicable_date, are derived from a single regex pass over rule_id_path; all three emit JSON null when the path does not match the canonical <rulesetid>_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<index>[, <rest>] shape
Key insertion order extended: rulesetid, applicable_date, rulesetid_index, rule_id_path, rule_id_path_key — identifier metadata grouped first, then the path and its derived stable key together

sections.title: Per-rulesetid aggregation
items: Response envelope now carries an aggregations.norms_per_rulesetid map alongside rules, listing the count of top-level rules per cprmv:rulesetId in the filtered result set
Counts are keyed by the authoritative cprmv:rulesetId value (not parsed from the path), so non-conforming rule_id_path values still aggregate correctly
Sum of values equals data.total, letting clients render ruleset-level summaries without a second pass over rules
Additive change — existing readers of data.rules and data.total see no breaking change

sections.title: Single source of truth for v1 routes
items: New backend module packages/backend/src/routes/registry.ts: every v1 route's mount path, router, summary and category lives in one array; adding a route is a one-line entry that both registration and the root page pick up automatically

Refactored packages/backend/src/routes/index.ts to iterate the registry for v1 mounting; legacy /api/* deprecation aliases stay hand-mounted (deprecated routes are intentionally excluded from the registry to steer consumers towards /v1/*)
Mount-order semantics preserved: more specific paths still precede their parents (/v1/chains/templates before /v1/chains) so Express route precedence behaves exactly as before

sections.title: Content-negotiated root page
items: GET / now serves HTML when Accept includes text/html (browsers) and JSON otherwise (curl, fetch with default Accept, programmatic pollers); both views are derived from the shared route registry so they cannot drift
HTML view groups endpoints by category (Health & monitoring, Discovery, Execution, Assets, Integrations) and badges public-CORS endpoints; styling is inline with no external dependencies

JSON payload preserves backwards compatibility: same top-level keys as before (name, version, environment, status, documentation, health, endpoints, legacy); existing programmatic clients see no breaking change
Closes the drift gap that was missing /v1/dso, /v1/norms, /v1/assets/*, /v1/cache, /v1/edocs, /v1/ropa, /v1/process and /v1/chains/templates from the previous hand-coded listing

sections.title: Deployment tier display label
items: New DEPLOYMENT_ENV environment variable distinguishes ACC from PROD when NODE_ENV is 'production' for both; falls back to NODE_ENV when unset so local development needs no change

Added config.displayEnv (string) and config.deploymentEnv (raw value) to packages/backend/src/utils/config.ts with mappings: prod/production → PROD, acc/acceptance/staging → ACC, dev/development/local → development, test → test, unknown values pass through
Used consistently by the HTML root page and the /v1/health response so the displayed environment stays in sync across surfaces
Configuration is per Azure App Service: az webapp config appsettings set ... --settings DEPLOYMENT_ENV=acc (or prod)

sections.title: New /v1/norms endpoint
items: New backend route GET /v1/norms exposing all cprmv:Rule paths and norms in the publish format consumed by the SPARQL editor's norm publisher
Response mirrors the cprmv-example.json shape exactly: fully-qualified RDF/CPRMV keys for type/id/definition/contains, short keys for situatie/norm/per/rulesetid/applicable_date/rule_id_path
Parent rules and their cprmv:contains children are aggregated into nested objects in a single response, with deterministic key ordering preserved across runs
Optional ?endpoint= query parameter overrides the default TriplyDB endpoint, matching the pattern already used by /v1/dmns

sections.title: Filtering by ruleset and applicable date
items: New applicable_date attribute derived from the _YYYY-MM-DD_ segment embedded in rule_id_path; null when no date is present in the path
Filter by ?rulesetid= (e.g. BWBR0015703) and/or ?applicable_date= (e.g. 2026-01-01); both parameters can be combined
Strict input validation against /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/ (rulesetid) and /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ (applicable_date) returns 400 INVALID_PARAM before any SPARQL fires
Validated filters are applied as SPARQL FILTER clauses (exact-match on rulesetId, CONTAINS on the dated segment of ruleIdPath) for server-side selection

sections.title: Maintenance
items: Silenced TypeScript 5.x deprecation warning on moduleResolution: "node10" via "ignoreDeprecations": "6.0" in packages/backend/tsconfig.json; full migration to nodenext deferred until ESM-on-Node maturity warrants the per-file .js extension changes

sections.title: Multilingualism — new
items: Language metadata on BPMN, Form, and Document artefacts (ISO 639-1: en, nl, de) — set via the editor footer panel; persisted to PostgreSQL and to BPMN XML as ronl:language; round-trips through export and import
Organization metadata on the same three artefact types — set via the editor footer with autocomplete from existing organizations; drives list-panel grouping
Language filter and free-text search across all three list panels (Processes, Forms, Documents)
Collapsible organization groups in all three list panels — subprocesses follow their shell's organization regardless of their own tag; orphan subprocesses (shell hidden by filter) render flat

Filename-based language inference on import — drop a capacity-claim-intake.nl.form into the form import and the language tag is applied automatically; XML and JSON wrapper values take precedence over filename inference
Form export now includes language and organization at the top of the JSON, plus a language-suffixed filename — round-trip integrity for all three artefact types
Deploy-time language consistency check — amber warning surfaces inline in the deploy modal when a bundle mixes languages, listing the offending codes; same UX as the existing RoPA-missing warning

All formRef and documentRef values in the Dutch BPMN suffixed -nl; flow labels (formatie, inhuur, akkoord, afgewezen, doorgaan, intrekken, werving, inkoop) translated; gateway condition expressions unchanged

Navigation guard with confirm prompt when leaving an artefact with unsaved changes (Create / Load another / Close)

Shell → subprocess atomic save — saving a shell propagates language and organization to all linked subprocesses in one write; idempotent (skips subprocesses already aligned); shell wins unconditionally
Save buttons now correctly reflect dirty state — Form Save was previously always-enabled (regression); now disables on load and after Save, enables on first edit

sections.title: Bug fixes
items: BPMN persistence: language and organization fields are now included in the BpmnService POST payload — previously dropped silently on the API call, causing values to vanish on hydration

OrganizationSelector input is now controlled (value/onChange) rather than uncontrolled (defaultValue/onBlur) — switching between artefacts now refreshes the input correctly; previous value no longer leaks across selections
BpmnCanvas no longer resets on every parent re-render — handleElementSelect stabilized via a ref, modeler-init effect deps narrowed to xml only

items: Database — language VARCHAR(2) and organization VARCHAR(100) columns added to process_definitions, form_schemas, and document_templates with partial indexes; nullable, existing rows coexist as NULL
BPMN moddle descriptor extended with LanguageMixin and OrganizationMixin on bpmn:Process — custom attributes survive saveXML round-trip via the existing ronl namespace
New shared components under packages/frontend/src/components/common/: LanguageSelector, OrganizationSelector, ArtefactListToolbar (with filterArtefacts helper)

Editor architecture — footer state lifted to the editor parent (BpmnModeler / FormEditor / DocumentComposer); children receive effective values via props and report changes via callbacks; Save is the single point of persistence

EXAMPLE_VERSIONS bumped for all existing examples to trigger one-time re-seed with organization tags; eleven new HR-capacity Dutch entries added at v1; organization keys standardized to lowercase (flevoland, toeslagen, bzk)

Each result shows the human-readable omschrijving, the functioneleStructuurRef (full concept URI — the Phase 4 pivot to STTR files), and the short werkzaamheid URN

Environment badge in the DSO Explorer header updates to reflect the active DSO environment (amber for pre-production, green for production)

Child activities in the detail panel now show human-readable names fetched in parallel after the parent detail loads
Graceful 404 handling in the detail panel: activities not available in the active DSO environment show a clear message instead of a raw error
Pagination unified to 20 items per page across both Concepts and Activities tabs

sections.title: Backend — DSO service
items: POST /v1/dso/activiteiten/oin — new endpoint wrapping _wijzigingen, accepts oin and optional datumVanaf, defaults to yesterday
X-Dso-Env request header added to all DSO frontend calls; backend reads it to select pre-production or production DSO config

dsoProd config block in config.ts: DSO_CATALOGUE_BASE_URL_PROD, DSO_RTR_BASE_URL_PROD, DSO_API_KEY_PROD environment variables
getDsoConfig() helper selects the correct base URL and API key per request
env parameter threaded through all dso.service.ts exported functions and logged with each DSO request

Concepts tab: full-text search across the Stelselcatalogus /begrippen endpoint — returns definitions, explanations, validity dates, and concept URIs

DSO Explorer header shows environment label (pre-production) to make the data context explicit

DsoActiviteitSelector footer panel in the BPMN Modeler (below RopaSelector): paste a URN, verify it live against the DSO RTR, and save it to the active process

sections.title: Public Bundle Library

A bundle is recorded at deploy time: shell or standalone BPMN process, Operaton deployment ID, Operaton URL, resolved form IDs, and resolved document template IDs are written to process_definitions

sections.title: PostgreSQL Asset Storage
items: BPMN processes, form schemas, and document templates now persist to PostgreSQL via the LDE backend — assets survive localStorage clearing and are shared across browsers and devices

Async hydration on editor mount: GET /v1/assets/ replaces non-readonly localStorage entries with authoritative server state on each page load

Example assets (readonly: true) are excluded from server writes — they remain seeded from public/examples/ as before
New backend routes: GET/POST /v1/assets/bpmn, GET/POST /v1/assets/forms, GET/POST /v1/assets/documents, DELETE /v1/assets/{type}/:id
New backend route GET /v1/assets/bpmn/by-bpmn-id/:bpmnProcessId for bundle assembly lookup by BPMN process id

sections.title: AWB Shell / Subprocess Hierarchy

SHELL and SUB role badges displayed on process cards for at-a-glance orientation

sections.title: Schema Versioning

sections.title: eDOCS Integration (Stub Mode)

Interaction Rules: informationRequirement href resolution, orphaned inputData detection, variable name consistency across DRD wiring
Content: non-empty CPRMV descriptive attributes, variable typeRef presence, non-empty textAnnotation content
